failure_observations.phenomenon: A soft-contact law or uncertainty model calibrated at one material, geometry, rate, or history does not preserve its force-prediction relation when relaxation, recovery, speed, surface motion, or material parameters change.
failure_observations.conditions: Held-out material stiffness or relaxation, thickness or curvature, scan speed or direction, dwell or loading history, or bounded surface motion differs from the calibration regime.

failure_observations.phenomenon: Finite-area deformation, pressure redistribution, tangential resistance, slip, and moment capacity change the admissible wrench relation beyond a scalar normal spring-damper description.
failure_observations.conditions: A rigid finite-area probe slides over a compliant surface while indentation, local geometry, velocity, friction, or contact patch evolves.

failure_observations.phenomenon: Online Cartesian stiffness and damping can be optimized under tracking-error and approximate gain constraints without representing the contacted environment, so the selected gains cannot condition on relaxation, hysteresis, pressure redistribution, or wrench capacity.
failure_observations.conditions: The selector receives robot dynamics and perturbation/tracking limits but no decision-sufficient soft-contact state.

failure_observations.phenomenon: Nominally desirable time-varying impedance can lose passivity or coupled stability and oscillate under constraint, while practical feedback improves stability at a free-space tracking cost.
failure_observations.conditions: Rendered impedance varies during constrained physical interaction and the environment or operator closes an energetic feedback path.

failure_observations.phenomenon: Contact-aware or uncertainty-tightened MPC can improve force and motion regulation while leaving impedance predefined, and scalar optimal impedance can improve identified one-dimensional contact while omitting finite-area wrench, passivity, and hard-limit coupling.
failure_observations.conditions: Prediction, uncertainty handling, or scalar impedance optimization is added as a separate component rather than solving the coupled online impedance decision under the complete constraint set.

phenomenon_clusters.grouping_rationale: Both observations show that held-out continuous contact changes the mapping from safely measured instantaneous variables to future force, tangential resistance, slip, and wrench capacity. The common failure is not generic model error but decision-relevant contact states becoming observationally aliased by a memoryless or calibration-fixed representation.

The gain selector, contact predictor, and constrained controller are each effective in their own variables, yet the causal relation from contact condition through feasible impedance to joint outcome is split across components. Consequently, prediction may not change gains and gain planning may not reflect contact capacity.

The abnormality concerns the energetic and stability consequences of changing impedance itself. It is distinct from prediction error: even a performance-improving gain can be unsafe or unrealizable when variation, constraint, and feedback energy are handled outside the selection relation.

why_steps.effect: Force, recovery, tangential resistance, and wrench-capacity predictions shift outside calibration.
why_steps.candidate_cause: Material relaxation, contact-area geometry, velocity, friction, and loading history alter the latent contact condition and its input-output relation.
why_steps.discriminating_observation: Under matched current pose, velocity, and wrench, changing prior dwell/loading or local patch geometry changes subsequent force relaxation, slip margin, or contact moment.

why_steps.effect: Different contact conditions are mapped to the same controller state or uncertainty estimate.
why_steps.candidate_cause: A scalar memoryless, preidentified, or static-output representation discards decision-relevant history and finite-area capacity coordinates.
why_steps.discriminating_observation: A history- or capacity-aware predictor separates paired conditions that are indistinguishable to the existing representation and reduces held-out conditional prediction error without additional future information.

why_steps.effect: The controller cannot preserve action-equivalence to the condition-informed impedance choice.
why_steps.candidate_cause: Aliased contact conditions induce different feasible or joint-cost-minimizing gains, but the fixed, scheduled, or contact-agnostic selector receives the same effective state and therefore returns the same action.
why_steps.discriminating_observation: An offline condition-informed oracle selects materially different normal or tangential stiffness/damping for aliased condition pairs and the action difference predicts joint outcome regret; if actions and outcomes remain equivalent, this step is false.

why_steps.effect: Online gain planning satisfies robot-side tracking and gain constraints but lacks contact-condition dependence.
why_steps.candidate_cause: The optimization state and constraints encode perturbation attenuation rather than soft-contact wrench capacity, relaxation, slip, or history.
why_steps.discriminating_observation: Adding only the contact-condition variables to a matched planner changes its chosen gains near held-out capacity or relaxation shifts; no action change falsifies this cause in that regime.

why_steps.effect: Contact prediction improves tracking without resolving which impedance should be selected.
why_steps.candidate_cause: Contact-aware and uncertainty-tightened MPCs retain predefined impedance, while identified optimal impedance is scalar and separated from finite-area contact feasibility.
why_steps.discriminating_observation: Holding the predictor fixed while optimizing normal and tangential gains changes outcomes beyond retuning the predefined gains; equivalence after exhaustive matched tuning weakens this explanation.

why_steps.effect: Constituent improvements do not compose into a verified online joint decision.
why_steps.candidate_cause: Prediction, impedance action, and hard feasibility are optimized or certified in separate relations, so no single decision variable is constrained by all force-motion-contact consequences at the update time.
why_steps.discriminating_observation: A jointly constrained reference changes the selected gain or fallback decision exactly when the separated stack would exceed wrench, energy, actuator, or deadline limits; identical decisions and limits falsify this step.

why_steps.effect: A time-varying impedance command can oscillate or lose coupled stability under constraint despite accurate nominal tracking.
why_steps.candidate_cause: Changing the rendered impedance exchanges energy with the interaction, and nominal gain desirability does not bound that exchange.
why_steps.discriminating_observation: Measured interaction-energy or passivity margin crosses its bound before constrained oscillation when the same performance gain is rendered without an energy gate.

why_steps.effect: A gain may be performance-improving but unavailable, unsafe, or late at the actual update instant.
why_steps.candidate_cause: Wrench/contact, interaction-energy, actuator, gain-rate, solver-time, infeasibility, and fallback constraints are not all part of the gain-selection feasibility relation.
why_steps.discriminating_observation: Enforcing the full constraint set during selection rejects or modifies gains that a performance-only planner accepts, and this prevents a registered hard-limit event without merely shifting failure to timeout or fallback.

causal_chains.conditions_or_input_change: Held-out material, relaxation, contact-area geometry, scan speed/direction, friction, dwell, loading history, or bounded surface motion changes during continuous finite-area scanning.
causal_chains.mechanism_failure: The controller state is not decision-sufficient: it aliases contact conditions with different future wrench/capacity relations, and the gain-selection relation is not conditioned on the missing distinction.
causal_chains.intermediate_state_abnormality: Contact prediction or uncertainty is biased or overconfident, slip/moment capacity is mislocated, and the same apparent state maps to an impedance action that is not action-equivalent to the condition-informed choice.
causal_chains.final_failure_phenomenon: The strongest simple baseline or separated predictor/planner exhibits excess joint force-motion-contact cost, contact loss or slip, hard-limit activation, or inability to select condition-dependent coupled normal-tangential stiffness and damping.

alternative_explanations.mechanism: Measured six-dimensional wrench feedback is already decision-sufficient; richer contact state changes prediction but not optimal gains or held-out outcomes.
alternative_explanations.discriminating_evidence: Under matched sensing, compute, tuning, and safety budgets, compare the strongest model-agnostic baseline with an offline contact-informed oracle on paired held-out conditions. Action and outcome equivalence supports this alternative.

alternative_explanations.mechanism: Observed regret comes from mismatched cost weights, tuning effort, horizons, or inner-loop bandwidth rather than missing contact state.
alternative_explanations.discriminating_evidence: Equalize objectives, tuning budget, horizon, inner loop, and compute; then test whether the state-conditioned action difference and residual persist.

alternative_explanations.mechanism: A well-calibrated memoryless finite-area model plus conservative uncertainty bounds fully captures all decision-relevant variation in the accepted envelope.
alternative_explanations.discriminating_evidence: Compare paired histories and geometries with identical instantaneous inputs; absence of conditional force/capacity and gain differences supports the memoryless explanation.

causal_chains.intervention_target: The causal relation from safely obtainable observations to a calibrated, decision-sufficient contact-capacity state used by impedance selection; retain additional history, geometry, area, tangential wrench, or uncertainty coordinates only when they change feasible gains or held-out outcomes.
causal_chains.falsifier: After matched objectives, compute, tuning, sensing, and safety, an oracle contact-capacity/history state neither changes the selected normal-tangential gains beyond equivalence margins nor improves any primary held-out outcome versus the strongest model-agnostic baseline.

causal_chains.conditions_or_input_change: Normal and tangential gains are updated online near wrench/contact, energy, actuator, gain-rate, or solve-time boundaries during constrained interaction.
causal_chains.mechanism_failure: Performance-oriented impedance selection and physical/real-time feasibility are separate relations, so the chosen gain is not jointly conditioned on rendered energy, contact capacity, actuator reachability, and deadline/fallback state.
causal_chains.intermediate_state_abnormality: A nominally low-cost gain injects excess interaction energy, approaches slip or moment limits, exceeds actuator or gain-rate capacity, or arrives after the online deadline; post-hoc guards then distort the intended action or force fallback.
causal_chains.final_failure_phenomenon: Constrained oscillation, wrench/contact violation, actuator saturation, timeout, infeasibility, fallback, or excess joint objective cost occurs even when the predictor or nominal gain optimizer performs well in isolation.

alternative_explanations.mechanism: A conservatively tuned fixed or scheduled impedance already stays within every hard limit and is outcome-equivalent; joint online feasibility adds no value.
alternative_explanations.discriminating_evidence: Use the strongest direct simple baseline with matched margins across all held-out axes; zero primary-endpoint loss and zero additional violations supports this alternative.

alternative_explanations.mechanism: Failures arise solely from solver implementation or hardware latency, not from the structure separating gain selection and feasibility.
alternative_explanations.discriminating_evidence: Compare an offline exact joint solution and a latency-matched online approximation. If the offline separated solution is feasible and outcome-equivalent, implementation latency is the better explanation.

alternative_explanations.mechanism: Standard post-hoc energy, saturation, and fallback guards project every nominal gain to the same feasible action a joint selector would choose.
alternative_explanations.discriminating_evidence: Log pre-guard and realized actions. Exact realized-action and outcome equivalence between post-hoc guarding and joint feasibility supports this alternative.

causal_chains.intervention_target: The impedance-decision feasibility relation itself: normal/tangential gain choice must be evaluated in the same update-time relation that accounts for wrench/contact capacity, interaction energy, actuator and gain-rate reachability, solve deadline, infeasibility, and deterministic fallback.
causal_chains.falsifier: With the same predictor, objectives, gains, and resource budget, coupling all hard constraints into the selection relation never changes the realized action or fallback decision and produces no improvement in violations or primary outcomes over a separated planner with standard post-hoc guards.

unresolved_questions: Which safely observable subset of contact area, local geometry, tangential force or moment, relaxation/history, and uncertainty is minimally sufficient to separate gain-relevant contact conditions?
On which held-out regimes does the strongest model-agnostic six-dimensional feedback baseline remain action- and outcome-equivalent, making richer state unnecessary?
Can decision-sufficient contact capacity be estimated at the slower impedance-update rate without unsafe excitation or violating the solve deadline?
Does joint update-time feasibility change gains and outcomes beyond standard post-hoc energy, saturation, uncertainty, and fallback guards, or merely reproduce them?
